  version    Show the version
  help       Show this help, or the help of a command: uiguide help <command>

result.stdout:
Usage: uiguide init [project folder or .csproj] [options]

Connects your application to a UiGuide Agent server:
  - writes uiguide.json next to the project, or updates the one the build created: only the server, the
    application id, the language and the key change; your other settings and comments stay,
  - checks that the server answers,
  - for a server on this computer, registers the application on it (data\apps\<appId>.json);
  - for another server (your company's): creates the application key (uiguide.json "key") and prints the
    one line to send to the server's administrator, who runs it there (uiguide-server app set ...).
Without options it asks; with --yes it uses the defaults.

Options:
  --server <url>        UiGuide Agent server (default http://localhost:5180)
  --app-id <id>         Application id: lowercase letters, digits, '-' (default: from the project name)
  --language <code>     Language of the assistant, e.g. de-DE (default: the application's UI culture)
  --description <text>  One sentence about what the application does (for the server profile)
  --origins <list>      Web: the pages allowed to use the server, comma separated (default: from the project — MAUI Blazor https://0.0.0.1, launchSettings.json, dev servers)
  --no-register         Do not register the application on the local server
  --yes                 Ask nothing, use the defaults

result.stdout:
Usage: uiguide scan [project folder or .csproj] [options]

Lists every button, menu, tab, input and list of the project without an accessible name: in WPF windows
(*.xaml), WinForms forms (*.Designer.cs) and controls created in C# code. The assistant sees only names
and ids, so it cannot point the user to a control without a name — the goal is that none is left.

Name each one after what it does, in the words a user would use for it:
  WPF        AutomationProperties.Name="Export orders"   (in code: AutomationProperties.SetName(button, "…"))
  WinForms   AccessibleName = "Export orders"
or by its text (Content, Header, Text) or label (<Label Target=…>, WinForms: the label before it in tab order).
Names are never invented. --fix only copies the tooltip / hint / inner text you already wrote in XAML or a
designer file — check that it says what the control does.

The build runs this too (when the project has uiguide.json): one warning UIG001 per control without a name,
with file and line. <WarningsAsErrors>UIG001</WarningsAsErrors> in the project makes them errors;
<NoWarn>UIG001</NoWarn> hides them.
Exit code 1 while controls are left without a name (use it in CI).

Options:
  --fix  Copy your own tooltip / hint / inner text into AutomationProperties.Name (XAML, designer; edits the files)
  --all  List the named controls too

result.stdout:
Usage: uiguide record --goal "<what the user wants>" [project folder] [options]

Starts your application (WPF / WinForms: the built .exe; other applications: through the Companion), records
the controls you use while you do the task once, and — when you close the application — adds the flow to
uiguide.map.json:  { "goal": "export the orders", "steps": [ "{fileMenuItem}", "{exportMenuItem}" ] }.
Only control ids, names and types are recorded: never what you type or which list item you pick.
Then build (or uiguide bundle) and the assistant knows the flow. Run again with the same goal to replace it.

Options:
  --goal <text>    What the user wants to do, in their words (e.g. "export the orders")
  --run <command>  Command line that starts the application (default: the built .exe; Python: python <main>.py)
  --from <file>    Use an existing recording file instead of starting the application
  --dry-run        Only show the steps, do not change uiguide.map.json

result.stdout:
Usage: uiguide bundle [project folder or .csproj] [options]

Generates uiguide.bundle.json — what the assistant knows about your application — from:
  - the code: windows (WPF x:Class, WinForms forms), their controls (id, type, name or resource key,
    menus nested, shortcuts) and the UI texts in every language (resource dictionaries, .resx);
  - uiguide.map.json (yours, optional): what controls do ("action"), when they are enabled
    ("enabledWhen"), which window they open ("opens"), and the "flows" (goal → steps).
    Your entries win over the generated ones for the same control (same automationId).
The file is rewritten only when something changed (no date inside: no needless diffs).
The first run creates an empty uiguide.map.json for you to fill.
The build does this at every build (.NET and the npm bundler plugins): run it yourself only for an
application without such a build (Python, Java, any exe with the Companion).

Usage: uiguide doctor [project folder or .csproj] [options]

Checks, in the order you set things up: the project, the UiGuideAgent.Desktop package, uiguide.json,
the server (version, protocol), its LLM, the registration of the application (server on this computer),
the knowledge bundle (valid, up to date with the code), accessible names, the WebView2 Runtime.
✔ ok   ! works, but could be better   ✖ must be fixed (exit code 1). Each problem says what to do.

result.stdout:
Usage: uiguide test [project folder] [options]

Asks every question of uiguide.tests.json to the server in uiguide.json (with your knowledge bundle) and checks
each answer: "expect" = texts it must contain (the exact names of your buttons / menus; "A|B" = either),
"avoid" = texts it must not contain. Comparison ignores case, quotes «» “” and "…" / "...".
  {
    "language": "en-US",
    "tests": [
      { "question": "How do I export the orders?", "screen": "main", "expect": [ "File", "Export to CSV" ] },
      { "question": "Wie ändere ich die Währung?", "language": "de-DE", "expect": [ "Settings|Einstellungen" ], "avoid": [ "Delete" ] }
    ]
  }
"screen" = the screen the user is on (id from the UI map); "context" = what UiGuide.SetContext would send.
Needs the server and its LLM running. Token: "key" in uiguide.json, or the UIGUIDE_TOKEN environment variable.

Options:
  --file <path>    Benchmark file (default uiguide.tests.json in the project)
  --server <url>   Another server than the one in uiguide.json (e.g. a test server)
  --filter <text>  Only questions containing this text
  --repeat <n>     Ask each question this many times; all must pass (stability, default 1)
  --timeout <s>    Seconds per answer (default 180)

result.stdout:
Usage: uiguide key [project folder] [options]

Creates a new application key:
  - on a server on this computer: apps\<appId>.json gets "auth": "AppKey" and the key's SHA-256 hash
    (another server: the one line to send to its administrator is printed),
  - the project's uiguide.json gets "key" (a web page gets it at the next build, in uiguide.config.json).
The key ships inside your application, so it identifies the application, not the user: set "limits" in
apps\<appId>.json. For signed-in users use "auth": "External" (the server checks the user's token with your
application). Run it again to rotate: the old keys keep working until you remove them from "keys".

Options:
  --app-id <id>   Application id (default: from the project's uiguide.json)
  --server <url>  UiGuide Agent server (default: from the project's uiguide.json)
  --no-config     Do not write the key into uiguide.json (only print it)

result.stdout:
Usage: uiguide update [project folder] [options]

Moves the project to the latest release:
  - .NET: dotnet add package UiGuideAgent.Desktop / UiGuideAgent.Web (the latest version);
  - web without .NET: npm install -D @ui-guide-agent/web@latest (the uiguide tool comes with it);
  - a web page with a copied ui-guide-agent.js: the file is replaced.
Then build and run. This tool itself (installed as a .NET tool): dotnet tool update -g UiGuideAgent.Cli
The server on this computer: dotnet tool update -g UiGuideAgent.Server.Host; Docker: docker pull, then docker run again.
You do not need to check for new releases: the build tells you (warning UIG002), with the line to run.

result.stdout:
Usage: uiguide remove [project folder] [options]

Takes UiGuide Agent out of the project:
  - the package reference (UiGuideAgent.Desktop / UiGuideAgent.Web),
  - uiguide.json and the generated uiguide.bundle.json,
  - the <script src="…ui-guide-agent.js"> line in your pages (web),
  - the application's registration and knowledge bundles on the local server
    (your company's server: the one line to send to its administrator is printed).
Kept unless --all: uiguide.map.json and uiguide.tests.json (you wrote them).
If your code calls the SDK (UiGuide.SetContext, uiGuide.start, …) nothing is changed: the calls are listed with
file and line — remove them first (the project would not build without the package), or use --force.
From this computer afterwards: dotnet tool uninstall -g UiGuideAgent.Server.Host (and UiGuideAgent.Cli,
UiGuideAgent.Companion); the server's settings and data are in the ui-guide-agent folder of your local
application data - delete it to remove them too.

Options:
  --all      Also delete uiguide.map.json and uiguide.tests.json
  --force    Remove even when code still calls the SDK (you fix the build)
  --dry-run  Only show what would be removed
